overview: Anaemia is a condition in which the number of red blood cells or the haemoglobin concentration within them is lower than normal, mainly affecting women and children. It occurs when there isn’t enough haemoglobin in the body to carry oxygen to the organs and tissues. In severe cases, anaemia can cause poor cognitive and motor development in children and problems for pregnant women and their babies.
symptoms: pale skin and under the fingernails
diagnosis: specified thresholds established based on age, sex, and physiological status
treatment: eating foods rich in iron, folate, vitamin B12, vitamin A, and other nutrients

key_facts: half a billion women 15–49 years of age are affected by anaemia worldwide
269 million children 6–59 months of age are affected by anaemia worldwide
106 million women and 103 million children are affected by anaemia in Africa
